prompt:
Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten figures of the same character, painted by hand. The first reference image gives the exact layout and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place and size of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the painting and the lighting change. The first reference is a plain grey 3D render: take only the layout and the poses from it, never its smooth plastic shading or its soft, even light. The second reference image only shows the costume, the face and the proportions of the character: do not copy its colours, its drawing style, its outlines or its three-view layout. The third reference image shows the black-and-white noir painting technique and the tonal range of the game: paint the figures with exactly this technique, but do not copy any of its content.

Painting technique: the same black-and-white film-noir painting as the background of the game (third reference): strictly monochrome, only black, white and neutral greys, with one single exception: the knitted scarf is a strong, saturated deep red, the only colour in the whole picture. Hard theatrical lighting, identical on all ten figures: a hard key light from the upper right and slightly in front (a street lantern ahead of the character) brightly lights the face, the chest, the parcel and the front leg; the back of each figure falls into deep, almost black shadow with a crisp, sharp-edged boundary; a thin bright white rim light runs along the top of the cap, the back of the head and the back. Clean, simplified painted shapes with crisp edges, few big tonal areas instead of fine texture: the fur in flat dark grey and light grey shapes, the broad black-and-white stripes of the face clearly readable, a small bright catchlight in the eye, the cap and the vest dark grey, the shirt light grey, satchel and parcel mid grey, the red scarf modelled only by light and shadow. No outlines, no fur texture, no individual hairs, no soft airbrush, no glossy plastic highlights, no colour except the red scarf. It must look like a painted character of a noir adventure game: not a 3D render, not a photograph, not a plush toy, not a cartoon with outlines.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Each figure isolated on a fully transparent background, with clear empty space between the figures; no ground, no cast shadow, no frame borders, nothing cut off at the edge of the sheet.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
